summary: This benchmark evaluates mechanistic attention steering in frozen Qwen2.5-72B by restricting attention masking to dictionary tokens before block 17. The methodology includes a well-matched syntax control and transparently documents that while the intervention yielded a statistically significant gain (+13.38 points over syntax control), it narrowly missed its pre-registered thresholds.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design incorporating a matched-size negative control (masking the preceding syntax token) to isolate semantic key reads from positional/structural masking artifacts.
Exemplary research integrity in preregistration and reporting, explicitly highlighting that the observed 78.34% switching rate and effect sizes missed registered targets (80% and +15 points).

Detailed runtime environment documentation, including exact software dependency versions, hardware parameters (Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GiB unified memory), peak memory allocation (146.71 GB), and execution wall-clock time.
Robust statistical reporting with paired 95% confidence intervals and conditioning across native-solved cohorts.
weaknesses: The manuscript is written as an extremely dense research memo (535 words) that omits broader qualitative context, prompt syntax examples, and baseline ablation analysis within the text itself.

Evaluation is restricted to a single model architecture (Qwen2.5-72B) and a single task domain (numeric dictionary lookup programs), leaving the generalizability of early key steering across other model families and task structures unverified.
No official supporting repository was linked in the submission metadata, restricting the verification badge to 'text_only' despite inline GitHub links.
suggestions: Include a concrete text snippet or diagram illustrating an example prompt, highlighting the 15 dictionary assignment tokens and the exact masked attention edges.
Extend the benchmark to other dense frontier open-weight models (e.g., Llama 3.3 70B) to determine if dictionary token key steering dynamics operate similarly at early transformer blocks.
Formally attach the verification repository in the submission metadata to enable automated code verification and eligibility for the 'verified_open' trust badge.

claims.text: exchange the 8,192-value key state with the paired prompt's state
The Studio run took 496 seconds, reaching 146.71 GB peak MLX allocation on Apple M5 Ultra with 80 GPU cores and 256 GiB unified memory.

Blocking the dictionary tokens from reading an early key before block 17 raised mirrored whole-state switching from 101 to 123 of 157 native-shared groups in frozen Qwen2.5-72B. An equal-size mask on the preceding syntax token switched 102.
claims.source: Mathematical and paired cohort verification: 123/157 = 78.34%, 102/157 = 64.97% (+13.38 points diff), 101/157 = 64.33% (+14.01 points diff)

novelty_vs_existing.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT (ROME)
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies causal intervention and hidden-state exchange specifically to multi-token dictionary parsing and attention edge masking in 70B+ scale open-weight LLMs rather than single-token MLP factual localization.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Causal Abstraction for Language Models
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Provides an empirical benchmark of targeted attention-edge cuts between variable definitions and syntax tokens on a standardized numerical lookup task with pre-registered effect-size thresholds.
